subject: Deployment mode qualification: shared vs dedicated - isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Deployment mode qualification: shared vs dedicated - isolation & SLOs

Hi Samir / Anita

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: synchronous checkout inference for fraud/score decisions (low-latency requirement).
- Current traffic profile: ~50 QPS steady, bursts up to ~200 QPS at peak.
- Target SLOs: P95 latency <= 150 ms, availability >= 99.9%.
- Concern: noisy neighbor/co-tenancy impacting tail latencies during heavy bursts.
- Data isolation: PCI-adjacent workloads, prefer strong isolation or contractual guarantees.

Open questions for you (will help us recommend the right deployment mode):
1) Can you confirm the percent of requests that are >512 tokens (affects KV-cache size)?
2) Any strict residency/KMS requirements (e.g., separate VPC or on-prem keys)?
3) Do you need per-tenant accounting or do you want cross-tenant pooling to reduce cost?

What we recommend next:
- Short technical deep-dive (30-45m) with Marissa to walk through the SLO target, traffic shapes, and capacity model.
- We'll run a lightweight benchmark that mirrors your payload (we can use your request payloads under an NDA) to show P95/P99 behavior on shared vs. dedicated pools.
- If dedicated looks necessary, we can produce a preliminary capacity quote and a canary rollout plan.

Attachments: redwood-isolation-slos.pdf (overview of isolation guarantees and benchmarking methodology)
Shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cSharedVsDedicatedDoc

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Wed 4/7 or Thu 4/8 between 9am-12pm PT. What works for you?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification: shared vs dedicated - isolation & SLOs

Thanks Priyom - really helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Token sizes: ~95% of requests are under 256 tokens; about 5% are 256-1024 tokens (mostly analytics calls).
- Residency/KMS: we require customer-managed keys for production (KMS in our AWS account).
- Accounting: we prefer per-tenant accounting but we are open to pooled billing if it comes with stronger SLO guarantees.

Our main ask: we need confidence that tails won't spike during high load. Last time we tested with another provider we saw P99 latency jumps to multiple seconds during neighbor spikes, which blocked checkout flows.

Can you confirm: 
1) On shared API, how do you mitigate noisy neighbor scenarios?
2) If we go Dedicated, what isolation guarantees and SLOs can Redwood commit to (or include in a contract)?
3) Rough ballpark price delta vs hosted shared API for the capacity numbers above?

We can do Wed 4/7 morning for the deep-dive. Also please send any benchmarks or docs you have that specifically address noisy neighbor behavior.

--Samir
Head of Engineering, FinPay

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification: shared vs dedicated - isolation & SLOs

Samir -

Really useful context, thanks. Quick answers to your questions and what we can do next: 

1) Shared API mitigation:
- Traffic shaping + per-customer async back-pressure and priority queuing for high-SLA routes.
- Smart batching and KV prefix caching to reduce per-token compute.
- We operate colocated pools and use continuous tail monitoring; when an anomalous noisy neighbor is detected we automatically route affected traffic to alternate healthy pools (soft isolation).
- Important: shared pools do not provide contractual isolation guarantees - they offer best-effort tail protections and are cost-optimized.

2) Dedicated capacity guarantees:
- Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool (no other customers on the same nodes) and configurable autoscale/burst policies.
- We can contract SLA targets for availability and standard latency SLOs at P95; for P99 we include monitoring and prioritized remediation SLOs. For stronger contractual isolation (e.g., dedicated NICs, VPC peering), we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or an on-prem variant.
- We can map your P95 <=150ms requirement to a capacity model and produce a draft SLA in the commercial proposal.

3) Ballpark pricing:
- Shared (hosted API): lowest unit cost, but no contractual isolation - best for teams that can tolerate soft tail mitigation.
- Dedicated: ~3-5x unit cost vs hosted (depends on GPU type and reserved commitment) for guaranteed throughput and isolation.
- Private: premium (license + infra) but gives full network/customer-managed KMS isolation.

Next steps I propose: 
- Marissa will run a short benchmark (we can use your 50 QPS steady / 200 QPS burst profile) across a shared pool and a small dedicated pool and share P95/P99 numbers.
- We\u2019ll include the redwood-isolation-slos.pdf (attached) and a simple capacity template (finpay-capacity-template.xlsx) to capture your traffic shapes and residency requirements.
- Schedule the deep-dive Wed 4/7 10:00 AM PT - Marissa, Vivek and I will join. Confirm and I\u2019ll send a calendar invite.

Attachment: redwood-isolation-slos.pdf, finpay-capacity-template.xlsx

Thanks,
